issue: `class Error < StandardError; end # note` fails the (?!.*\bend\s*$) lookahead and opens a nested body (strip_comments blanks whole-line comments only). The skip ends at the next indent-matching `end`, which closes the component's own initializer, so the component reads as 'defines no initializer'. On dev it is clean. Same at scripts/check_component_passthrough.py:65. Fix: drop a trailing `# ...` before the one-liner test and before the closer test, and add a fixture.

A nested class closed by `end # Section` never matches line.strip()=='end', so the skip runs to the end of the body and the component's `**attrs` initializer vanishes: 'defines no initializer' (dev gave a different wrong answer, 'fixed keyword list'). The CHANGELOG says each nested body ends 'at the `end` at its own indent', which does not hold for this common style. Same at scripts/check_component_passthrough.py:80. Fix: compare line.split('#')[0].strip() == 'end'; add a fixture.

A heredoc line starting `class Foo` opens a nested body and swallows the initializer after it: 'defines no initializer' at head, clean on dev. Rare in components. Fix: skip heredoc bodies, or accept the gap and document it.

A `Struct.new(...) do`, `Data.define(...) do` or `Class.new do` block above the component's initializer still has its `def initialize(` judged: 'fixed keyword list', the #1434 defect in another shape. Retask's TableComponent already uses Struct.new. Extend own_lines to `= (Struct.new|Data.define|Class.new)...do` openers, or state the limit in the CHANGELOG.

No fixture asserts that a component whose ONLY initializer is inside a nested class is reported as 'defines no initializer'. The probe shows it is reported, but nothing pins it. Add a fixture to both selftests.

The class-regex mutation is caught by an assertion that combines the `class:` case with the blank-line case, and the guard names the `class:` label. Split the assertion so each mutation fails its own label.
own_lines/NESTED are copied verbatim into two files, and nothing asserts the copies stay identical. R1 and R2 need fixing in both. Add a sameness check, or a comment naming the twin.

Tabs, `class << self` holding `def initialize`, and module-in-class deep nesting all behave correctly (probe), but no fixture covers them. Add fixtures so a later regex edit cannot regress them silently.
